requirements.basis: The complete current report substantively answers the original task. It defines representative industrial loading, logistics transfer/unloading/picking and household manipulation tasks by objects, environment, actions, cadence and failure consequences, with dedicated automation as a real alternative. Its route/data matrix separates modular, learned end-to-end, VLA, world-model and hybrid responsibilities and identifies hardware, tooling, controls and human complements. Data sections distinguish demonstrations, logs, correction, synthetic action data and simulation and discuss acquisition labor, calibration, coverage, distribution shift and held-out evaluation. The runtime chapter addresses stale observations, network delay, local control, independent safety and recovery rather than outsourcing them to high-level reasoning. The deployment matrix retains stages, dates, denominators and missing intervention/quality data; BMW hardware changes, Ocado/Kroger network contraction and remote-assisted household service supply concrete counterevidence without pretending to isolate a single cause. Relevant original passages confirm the Figure forearm hardware-learning account, Kroger's network financial shortfall, and pi0.5's task-progress/10-trial and training-mixture distinctions. The full economics section has explicit hypothetical inputs, demand-capped qualified output, availability, utilization, recovery labor, installation, maintenance, software, consumables, training, on-site support and realizable labor value, with lifetime/intervention/utilization sensitivities and an explicit discussion of downtime losses. It does not pass scenario results off as vendor ROI. The final industrial/logistics/household conditions and feedback loop use the preceding evidence and include cases for dedicated systems or deferred deployment. R_TASK matches the original case prompt, and the task report equals the frozen review text. No missing answer, scope drift or lost instruction requiring revision was found within requirements review; this is not a substitute for independent line-by-line evidence or domain assessment.
